A Blog post by IBM Research on Hugging Face
A Blog post by IBM Research on Hugging Face
There are nearly 200 agent harnesses to choose from. We gave three of them the same open-weight model and 90 AppWorld tasks, and changing the harness moved task completion from 30% to 81%. For enterprise use, CUGA adds what this benchmark does not test: rules that the harness enforces and deployment inside your own boundary.
Community lists such as awesome-agent-harness and best-of-Agent-Harnesses track nearl

en.reason: Holding the model constant across 90 AppWorld tasks, IBM Research's three-harness comparison of CUGA, Hermes and Deep Agents moved completion from 30% to 81%, with CUGA pitched at enterprises needing enforced rules and in-boundary deployment.

Prices for smuggled HBM3E memory have surged to around $4,000 per unit in just one year.

en.reason: Huawei is telling customers to source HBM for its AI chips themselves, as U.S. rules block Samsung and SK Hynix, over 80% of the market, while smugglers bundle HBM through Hong Kong and HBM3E prices reach about $4,000 a unit.

items.title: DeepSeek这次，想把你从AI的监工岗位上解放出来
items.summary: 老金这篇文章把 Super-agent 的机制讲得很直白：Router 像调度员，记住任务关系并分派；Worker 在各自会话里并行执行，耗时操作转后台，独立检查者盯进度和跑偏。它用更多计算换更短、更稳的等待，但公开原型仍偏实验，需配 Harness、独立账号和隔离环境，主动任务先观察、代码先人工合并。

en.title: This time, DeepSeek wants to free you from the job of supervising AI
en.summary: Lao Jin’s article lays out the Super-agent mechanism plainly: the Router acts as a dispatcher, remembering task relationships and assigning work; Workers execute in parallel in their own sessions, time-consuming operations get moved to the background, and independent checkers monitor progress and drift. It trades more compute for shorter, steadier waits, but the public prototype is still experimental and requires a Harness, separate accounts, and isolated environments. Proactive tasks should be observed first, and code should be merged manually first.
en.reason: DeepSeek’s Super-agent design exploration pairs a Router that dispatches tasks with parallel Workers and an independent checker, demoing an agent that adds a font-size setting to the same PR and reports the merge back to group chat.

items.summary: 这一周的精选 AI论文有个很明显的信号：AI 系统开始从“把更强模型塞进更多 Agent”，转向让检索、验证、记忆和模型协作各自做更确定的事。想把 Agent 做稳的人，这批研究比单纯看模型榜单更有参考价值。

en.title: 10.26–11.1 | This Week's Best AI Papers
en.summary: This week's curated AI papers send a clear signal: AI systems are moving away from "stuffing stronger models into more Agents" and toward making retrieval, verification, memory, and model collaboration each do more deterministic work. For anyone trying to build Agents that hold up, these studies are more useful than simply scanning model leaderboards.
en.reason: DecisionRAG's decision-model layered retrieval beats dense retrieval plus an 8B reranker by 13.8 R@1 points on MultiDoc2Dial at 0.7–1.8 seconds per query, while Unified Training unifies pretraining through RL under one likelihood algorithm in this week's selected AI papers.

en.title: AI changes the data interface, not the query engine
en.summary:
This article walks through a disaster recovery analysis workflow: an AI agent generates constrained SQL or Python code, DuckDB computes reproducible facts from Parquet files, and the agent then interprets the results.

Word count: 6,478 words
Reading time: about 21 minutes

AI agents can embed lightweight query engines such as DuckDB into operations analysis to produce end-to-end structured reports without relying on a traditional lakehouse architecture. The key is decoupling deterministic computation (metric aggregation) from probabilistic reasoning (fault attribution), then choosing an embedded engine or a managed lakehouse based on actual needs.

Key points: embedded engines suit low-latency, deterministic aggregation plus small-scale reasoning; lakehouses remain necessary for cross-team sharing, high-concurrency SQL, long-term governance, and compliance audits. The decision criteria include data freshness, collaboration breadth, computational determinism, and governance requirements.

Intended for SRE engineers, data platform architects, and AI engineering leads.

AI agents can now generate analysis code, read files from object storage, and turn operational data into structured reports. Does this mean data lakes, lakehouses, and SQL engines are obsolete? In our...
en.reason: Using a 30-second-granularity disaster recovery drill, the workflow has AI agents generate constrained SQL or Python while DuckDB computes reproducible facts from Parquet files, and gives four criteria for choosing an embedded engine versus a managed lakehouse.

en.title:
The "intelligent agent" dream from 25 years ago is coming true today — just in a different way

On November 2, MIT Technology Review published a long feature, The Agent Web Has Arrived (https://t.co/rVUmupywZn): today's AI assistants can sort email, compare prices, book restaurant tables and flights, and some are even authorized to access inboxes; websites are also starting to serve content to both humans and AI agents.

en.title: This time, DeepSeek wants to free you from the job of supervising AI
en.summary: Lao Jin’s article lays out the Super-agent mechanism plainly: the Router acts as a dispatcher, remembering task relationships and assigning work; Workers execute in parallel in their own sessions, time-consuming operations get moved to the background, and independent checkers monitor progress and drift. It trades more compute for shorter, steadier waits, but the public prototype is still experimental and requires a Harness, separate accounts, and isolated environments. Proactive tasks should be observed first, and code should be merged manually first.
en.reason: DeepSeek’s Super-agent design exploration pairs a Router that dispatches tasks with parallel Workers and an independent checker, demoing an agent that adds a font-size setting to the same PR and reports the merge back to group chat.

en.title: AI changes the data interface, not the query engine
en.summary:
This article walks through a disaster recovery analysis workflow: an AI agent generates constrained SQL or Python code, DuckDB computes reproducible facts from Parquet files, and the agent then interprets the results.

Word count: 6,478 words
Reading time: about 21 minutes

AI agents can embed lightweight query engines such as DuckDB into operations analysis to produce end-to-end structured reports without relying on a traditional lakehouse architecture. The key is decoupling deterministic computation (metric aggregation) from probabilistic reasoning (fault attribution), then choosing an embedded engine or a managed lakehouse based on actual needs.

Key points: embedded engines suit low-latency, deterministic aggregation plus small-scale reasoning; lakehouses remain necessary for cross-team sharing, high-concurrency SQL, long-term governance, and compliance audits. The decision criteria include data freshness, collaboration breadth, computational determinism, and governance requirements.

Intended for SRE engineers, data platform architects, and AI engineering leads.

en.title:
The "intelligent agent" dream from 25 years ago is coming true today — just in a different way

On November 2, MIT Technology Review published a long feature, The Agent Web Has Arrived (https://t.co/rVUmupywZn): today's AI assistants can sort email, compare prices, book restaurant tables and flights, and some are even authorized to access inboxes; websites are also starting to serve content to both humans and AI agents.
en.reason: AI assistants can now sort email, compare prices and book restaurants and flights—some are granted email access—as MIT Technology Review’s November 2 article cites Pew research that AI summaries cut site click-throughs by about 40%.
